//: TRI-RUNTIME BEHAVIOURAL FIXTURE for the maneuver-planner command surface. Every case here is byte-diffed across the browser harness, native WasmEdge and the pinned Docker WasmEdge, at 1/2/4/8 threads. Success paths AND failure paths: a deterministic error is parity evidence exactly like a deterministic answer. Until 0.2.0 this module's failure path was a TRAP (its exceptions were compiled out) and the cases below expected the trap CLASS to match across lanes. 0.2.0 gave the module a real error path, so those same cases now expect "guest-error" — the SAME inputs, judged by the same instrument, with the expectation flipped in the commit that flipped the behaviour. Run: space-data-module parity --wasm dist/isomorphic/module.wasm --fixture parity/maneuver-command.json --lanes browser,wasmedge,docker-wasmedge
name: maneuver-command-parity

cases.//: The canonical case the program pins. Also the tightest possible parity probe: a closed-form answer that is a handful of sqrt() calls, so any divergence between lanes is a libm difference and nothing else.

Positive phase angle: the phasing orbit is SMALLER and the first burn is retrograde. The response carries only the magnitude, so what this case pins across lanes is that phasingSMA — the quantity the console wrapper recovers the sign from — is byte-identical everywhere.

170 degrees in one revolution. 0.1.0 returned a phasing orbit whose far apse was ~4,300 km BENEATH the surface, with no error and no flag, and this case existed to pin that the DEFECT was reproduced identically on all three runtimes so the console-side guard was known to be guarding the same behaviour everywhere. 0.2.0 clamps to Re+100 km and says so (clampedToEarthFloor, farApse, achievedPhaseAngle), so what is pinned now is the GUARD: the clamp must fire at the same input and produce the same numbers on every lane.

Tudat's elliptical Lambert case. In 0.1.0 this was the one geometry the solver got right, included so the parity lane would already be watching the operation when the defect was repaired. It is repaired: solveLambert is a bracketed, residual-checked universal-variable solve and all four Tudat rows arrive. This case now also pins `converged` and `residual`, which are measurements rather than the literal `true` 0.1.0 returned on every path.

An unknown operation returns errorCode "unknown-operation" and a JSON {error, errorCode} body, identically on every lane. Under 0.1.0 this aborted the guest and poisoned the instance. EXIT CLASS IS "ok", NOT "guest-error": the command surface always exits 0 and encodes the refusal INTO the PIV response envelope ({error, errorCode} plus the module's message). That makes "ok" the stronger expectation here, because an "ok" case is additionally BYTE-DIFFED across every lane and thread count — so the whole error payload, message text included, is pinned rather than just the class. What changed at 0.2.0 is that this input used to produce class "trap".

An antipodal geometry: r1 and r2 exactly opposed, so every plane through the line is a valid transfer plane and no unique solution exists. The universal-variable formulation says so algebraically (A = 0). 0.1.0 answered converged:true here.
